I've drawn the architecture figure for experiment 22 and written it to `runs/20261102_045316_experiment22/figure.json`. I rendered it and looked at the picture, and figcheck prints PASS.

I started from experiment 20's figure, because the design record says the model itself is unchanged and only the training signal changed:

- **What flies is unchanged, all in ink:** two EfficientNet-B0 trunks, cosine tile matching against belief fields A and B, their averaged belief, the pooled 3×3 centroid, and the min(mA, mB) confidence gate. The camera frame and the (lat, lon, confidence) output sit level on the centre line, in grey, tagged "frozen contract".
- **Red, the one change (continuous vantages):** a 3×3 piece of the 24 px training lattice. Each lattice point (grey dot) has a dashed ±12 px box around it, and the boxes tile the ground with no gaps. Red crosses mark jittered vantages scattered inside them, and one shifted crop window shows a single sample. Next to it, a short text block says the offset is redrawn every time a spot is used, the same shift applies to all three surveys, and the tile and offset targets follow the shifted centre. A dashed leader runs from the glyph to trunk B.
- **Weight averaging, which was red in experiment 20, is now an unchanged training element.** It moved into the gold training text as "weight averaging epochs 5–8, BN stats re-measured".
- **Footer:** it now reads "only where training views stand changed · … identical to exp 20".

The rendered preview is `fig.png`, next to the output file, along with the helper script that builds the figure.
